newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Britain, China near accord on 1997-98 HK budget.
newsitem.headline: Britain, China near accord on 1997-98 HK budget.

text.p: British and Chinese negotiators said on Thursday they had basically finished drawing up Hong Kong's government budget for the coming fiscal year, which straddles the territory's return to China.

"We have basically completed the detailed compilation of the 1997-98 budget," said Hong Kong Treasury Secretary K.C. Kwong, who headed the British team to the expert level talks of the Sino-British Joint Liaison Group (JLG).
"This has been a process through which both parties have cooperated in a positive, pragmatic and constructive manner," he told reporters.
The two sides will meet again on March 4.
Chinese team leader Chen Zuo'er said the budget produced by the expert meetings would be finalised through the appropriate legislative process, China's official Xinhua news agency reported.
Hong Kong's Financial Secretary traditionally gives his budget speech in March.
The fiscal year starts on April 1. Hong Kong reverts to China at midnight on June 30.
The JLG was formed to thrash out transitional issues.
China has promised Hong Kong fiscal autonomy after the handover but has insisted on having a say in the 1997-98 budget covering the transition.
